issue_asks: Built-in extension usable as markdown.markdown(text, extensions=['strikethrough'])
Other inline markup (bold, emphasis, links) works inside the strikethrough
A single ~ or an unclosed ~~ is left alone
Off unless the extension is enabled (default behaviour unchanged)

findings.problem: Runs of three or more tildes are not treated as literal as they are on GitHub. Three tildes leave a stray tilde on each side of the <del>. Four tildes give nested <del><del>. The issue does not mention this and it is an unlikely input, so it does not block.

reviewer.summary:
The change adds a `strikethrough` extension that registers a `~` delimiter, with `smart=False` and `double=True`, on the existing `em_strong` DelimiterProcessor. When no such processor exists it registers its own at priority 60. This matches how `legacy_em` extends the processor. It is registered in the `pyproject.toml` entry points, documented, and the changelog and docs navigation are updated. The full suite passes (1192 tests). My own probes confirmed the following:

- `~~a~~` gives `<del>a</del>`.
- Nested bold, em, links, code spans and raw HTML work inside `<del>`.
- `**bold ~~x~~**` works.
- A single `~`, an unclosed `~~`, and `~~ a~~` or `~~a ~~` with whitespace next to the tildes stay literal.
- Overlapping spans with `*` or `**` degrade sanely.
- It works with legacy_em, smarty, tables and fenced_code, in either load order.
- It is off by default, and a reused Markdown instance resets correctly.

The one small deviation from GitHub is that runs of three or more tildes are not treated as literal. The tests in the diff are new and check what the issue asks for. No existing tests were removed or weakened.

decision.why: every checklist item is true and there is no blocker/major finding
